messages:
sam (acme-poc): Hey team, quick heads-up: during the customer walkthrough at ~14:03 PDT we saw ~12% 5xx on the completes endpoint for about 45s. Demo tanked a bit. Can someone look?

nina (sales): Oof, sorry about that. Are these returning 503s or 500s? Any x-request-id we can paste?

sam (acme-poc): Mostly 503. Example response:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 21:03:12 GMT
x-rd-error: capacity_throttle
x-request-id: req_ff3a9d11
content-type: application/json

{"error":"capacity_throttle","message":"no available slot"}
```

tasha (support): capacity_throttle header suggests serving-side soft throttling. Was this route configured with any strict_quality flags or fallback disabled?

sam (acme-poc): I double-checked the POC config earlier — we set strict_quality: true because they wanted consistent model outputs for the security review. No fallback enabled.

fergus (eng-runtime): That explains it. With strict_quality on we don't route to cheaper variants even under pressure. Did the autoscaler spin up? I can check logs for req_ff3a9d11.

liam (eng-sre): Cluster metrics show queue growth at 21:03:10, live_workers=4, max_workers=4. Autoscaler fired but new workers didn't register until 21:03:28. The backlog peaked and runtime began rejecting.

fergus (eng-runtime): Log snippet for the request id:

```
[21:03:12.104] WARN runtime::throttle capacity_throttle queue_len=31 workers=4/4
[21:03:12.110] ERROR runtime::accept reject req_ff3a9d11 no_slot
[21:03:12.867] INFO autoscale request desired=8 current=4 reason="queue_growth"
```

nina (sales): Customer already emailed saying they noticed "service glitch" during the sensitive demo. They'll escalate on the contract. Any quick mitigations we can perform now?

liam (eng-sre): Immediate mitigations: 1) enable tenant-level fallback (will allow cheaper variant); 2) temporarily increase burstpool headroom for this POC; 3) reduce autoscale cooldown to let workers register faster. I can apply 2) now if approved.

sam (acme-poc): They want no silent model swaps during the security review. If fallback is enabled it must be visible. Can we add a header or a response code change so we know when fallback happened?

fergus (eng-runtime): Yes — when fallback routes we set x-rd-fallback: true and x-model-variant. Also we can include x-rd-fallback-reason: degraded_capacity. That will still return 200 unless the fallback model errors.

nina (sales): Pricing question from the customer: will increasing burstpool or pre-warm add extra charges? They asked about per-minute cost or committing to dedicated headroom.

tasha (support): Short answer: burstpool minutes are billed as usage on Dedicated POCs — I'll pull the exact SKU and give a ballpark. For demos we can enable a short pre-warm window with minimal cost; I'll send pricing notes to the customer.

liam (eng-sre): I've applied a temporary bump: burstpool +5 and autoscale cooldown -> 7s for pool poc-789. Should reduce further 5xx in immediate window. Monitor dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/poc-789/pool (internal link).

sam (acme-poc): I can confirm the demo harness is now back to healthy; error rate dropped to <1%. Thanks.

fergus (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-9876 opened to investigate 15-30s registration delay (probable image warm/JIT). I'll include the model artifacts and node boot logs. Also will add a feature request to make fallback-visible-by-default for demo routes.

nina (sales): I'll consolidate a short note to the buyer: what we changed (burstpool bump, autoscale tweaks), fallback semantics (headers + visible routing), and a cost estimate for pre-warm minutes.

ops-bot: policy-change applied to pool poc-789 by liam  burstpool_headroom=+5 cooldown_seconds=7

tasha (support): I'll update the POC runbook snippet with exact headers to look for and the mitigation checklist. Closing the support thread; will follow up with the runbook and the pricing blurb. :white_check_mark:
